my_sentence: I went to the company, finished to finish my task.
correction: I went to the company and finished my task.
explanation: After the verb 'finished,' use the noun phrase 'my task,' not an infinitive. The two verbs can also be joined with 'and.'
correct_examples: I went to the office and finished my report.
She finished her work before dinner.

my_sentence: Then I back to home.
correction: Then I came back home.
explanation: The past-tense verb 'came' is needed. We usually say 'come back home' without 'to' before 'home.'
correct_examples: I came back home at seven.
She came home after work.
context: Describing what he did after work.

my_sentence: I eat my dinner.
correction: I ate my dinner.
explanation: The question asks about a completed meal, so use the past tense 'ate,' not the present tense 'eat.'
correct_examples: I ate dinner at home.
We ate our lunch together.

my_sentence: I eat some noodles.
correction: I ate some noodles.
explanation: Use the past tense 'ate' because the meal had already happened.
correct_examples: I ate some noodles for dinner.
He ate rice and vegetables.
context: Saying what he ate for dinner.

my_sentence: That need to be finished in afternoon and I forgot our assignments assessment.
correction: That needed to be finished in the afternoon, and I forgot the assignment.
explanation: Use past tense 'needed' for the past situation, add 'the' before 'afternoon,' and use the singular noun 'assignment' for one task.
correct_examples: The report needed to be finished in the afternoon.
I forgot the assignment.
context: Explaining why the homework was forgotten.

my_sentence: I will appreciate for your help.
correction: I would appreciate your help.
explanation: The collocation is 'appreciate your help,' without 'for.' In a polite request, 'would appreciate' is natural.
correct_examples: I would appreciate your help with this report.
We would appreciate your feedback.

my_sentence: I need ask some help.
correction: I need to ask for help.
explanation: After 'need,' use 'to' plus the base verb. The collocation is 'ask for help,' not 'ask help.'
correct_examples: I need to ask for help.
She asked for help with the task.

my_sentence: I only generous to my family.
correction: I am only generous to my family.
explanation: The adjective 'generous' needs the linking verb 'am' after the subject 'I.'
correct_examples: I am generous to my family.
She is generous to her colleagues.
context: Discussing whether he is a generous person.

my_sentence: You need to ask your boss to get a permission.
correction: You need to ask your boss to get permission.
explanation: Permission is normally an uncountable noun in this expression, so do not use the article 'a.'
correct_examples: You need permission to enter.
She asked her manager for permission.

my_sentence: They went to the lawyers office to get a divorce.
correction: They went to the lawyer's office to get a divorce.
explanation: Use the possessive form 'lawyer's' because the office belongs to or is associated with the lawyer.
correct_examples: I went to the doctor's office.
They visited the lawyer's office.

my_sentence: We plan to go to a park to have a meal.
correction: We plan to go to a park to have a picnic.
explanation: A meal eaten outdoors in a park is usually called a 'picnic.' The teacher suggested this more natural expression.
correct_examples: We went to the park to have a picnic.
They had a picnic by the lake.

my_sentence: You need to stop your work and had a rest.
correction: You should stop working and have a rest.
explanation: After 'should,' use the base form 'stop.' After 'stop,' use the gerund 'working,' and coordinate it with 'have.'
correct_examples: You should stop working and have a rest.
We stopped working and took a break.

my_sentence: Yesterday I had an argument with my classmates. We can't understand each other the ideas.
correction: Yesterday I had an argument with my classmates because we couldn't understand each other's ideas.
explanation: Use the possessive reciprocal form 'each other's' before 'ideas.' Because the event was yesterday, use 'couldn't' for the past situation.
correct_examples: We couldn't understand each other's ideas.
The two teams understood each other's concerns.

my_sentence: Before going to the bed, you'd better to take a shower.
correction: Before going to bed, you should take a shower first.
explanation: The fixed expression is 'go to bed' without an article. After 'should,' use the base verb 'take,' not 'to take.'
correct_examples: I take a shower before going to bed.
You should go to bed early.

my_sentence: When we finished our dinner, I'd like to go out to take a walk.
correction: When we finish eating our meal, I'd like to go out for a walk.
explanation: For a repeated or planned situation, use present tense 'finish.' The natural expression is 'finish eating our meal' and 'go out for a walk.'
correct_examples: When we finish eating, I like to go for a walk.
We went for a walk after finishing our meal.

my_sentence: My family members often take a trip, but to different cities or place.
correction: My family members often take trips to different cities or places.
explanation: Use the plural forms 'trips,' 'cities,' and 'places' for repeated travel to more than one location. Use 'to' to introduce the destinations.
correct_examples: My family members often take trips to different cities.
We take trips to different places every year.

my_sentence: I have many work.
correction: I have a lot of work.
explanation: Work is uncountable in this meaning, so use 'a lot of work' rather than 'many work.'
correct_examples: I have a lot of work today.
She has too much work this week.

my_sentence: It's very important to learn how to take responsibilities that can help you get a promotion.
correction: It's very important to learn how to take responsibility because that can help you get promoted.
explanation: Use the uncountable expression 'take responsibility.' Here the result is expressed naturally with 'get promoted,' not 'get a promotion.'
correct_examples: Taking responsibility can help you get promoted.
Good employees take responsibility for their work.

my_sentence: Even though the project is very difficult, he decided to take a risk.
correction: Even though the project is very difficult, he decides to take a risk.
explanation: The exercise required the simple present, so use 'decides' for the third-person singular subject 'he.'
correct_examples: He decides to take a risk despite the difficulty.
She decides carefully before accepting a challenge.

my_sentence: Dina wants to take control of her own life because he wants to go away with their parents.
correction: Dina wants to take control of her own life because she plans to go away with her parents.
explanation: Use pronouns that agree with the female subject Dina: 'she' and 'her,' not 'he' and 'their.'
correct_examples: Dina wants to control her own life.
She plans to travel with her parents.

my_sentence: No matter who need help.
correction: No matter who needs help.
explanation: In this clause, 'who' refers to one person at a time, so use the third-person singular verb 'needs.'
correct_examples: I help no matter who needs help.
Call me if anyone needs help.

my_sentence: When I try to fix some problems, I find the time went flying.
correction: When I try to fix something, I find that time flies so fast.
explanation: Use the present-tense expression 'time flies' for a general experience. The natural phrase is 'time flies so fast,' not 'time went flying.'
correct_examples: When I work on a difficult problem, time flies.
I find that time flies when I am busy.
context: Talking about how quickly time passes while working.

my_sentence: It's very important for him to make a choice to write a school.
correction: It's very important for him to make a choice to select the right school.
explanation: The intended verb is 'select,' not 'write.' Use the determiner 'the' before 'right school' when referring to the suitable choice.
correct_examples: He needs to select the right school.
Choosing the right college is important.

my_sentence: He is to study hard to get a high score.
correction: He needs to study hard to get a high score.
explanation: The sentence needs the modal-like expression 'needs to' to express necessity; 'he is to study' does not fit this meaning.
correct_examples: He needs to study hard for the exam.
You need to practice to improve your score.
context: Explaining how a student can become a doctor.

my_sentence: Tomorrow will be rain.
correction: It can rain tomorrow.
explanation: Use the dummy subject 'it' with weather expressions and the verb 'rain.' The modal 'can' expresses a possibility.
correct_examples: It may rain tomorrow.
It can rain heavily in August.
